html: Check the PL92T box before buying accessories: Lelit lists a 35 L water-softener filter, blind basket, first-cleaning kit and 9–11 g and 14–18 g IMS baskets. The filter capacity is not a universal replacement interval; test your water and follow its instructions. Ask a used-machine seller which accessories remain. PL92T3 has a separate equipment list. Checked October 26, 2026. [source]
note: Lelit PL92T factory page lists the supplied 35 L filter, blind basket, cleaning kit and basket capacities.

html: Verify the TCA name on the offer: Rocket now publishes a separate updated non-TCA Appartamento page as well as the Appartamento TCA. The non-TCA page describes eight finishes, a deeper tray and RGB status lights, but lists no PID pressure control or shot timer; the TCA page lists five finishes and its temperature-control adjustment. A newer-looking Appartamento photograph or a shared circular side-panel design does not establish that a listing includes TCA's four thermal presets. Confirm the exact model plate and control instructions with the seller. Checked October 26, 2026. [source]
note: Rocket's current non-TCA Appartamento page differs from its separate TCA page in finish count and control specification.

html: Do not copy ECM's two-second flush as a fixed recipe: the current Mechanika VI Slim and Slim PID manual gives approximate post-warm-up brew ranges for its three boiler settings, but says its two-second test flush was chosen for comparable measurements. It advises adjusting a real flush to bubbling or hissing; a longer or shorter flush changes brew temperature. Record idle time, switch position and flush behavior with one coffee before interpreting a sharp or roasty shot as a grinder fault. These are ECM's guide ranges, not Coffeedant group-temperature measurements. Checked October 26, 2026. [source]
note: ECM manual distinguishes three boiler setpoints and approximate post-flush brew ranges, and says two seconds was only its comparable test flush.

html: Move back toward espresso with the motor running: Clive's exact Zero 65 AP operating guide says a fine-to-coarse move can be made stopped, but a large coarse-to-fine return is best made while grinding to avoid a jam. It suggests small quarter- to half-number changes when dialing espresso. The marked revolution counter helps relocate a starting point; it does not guarantee the same particle distribution after a different bean or cleaning. If grounds stop flowing, open the burrs toward coarse as the guide directs rather than forcing a finer setting. Checked October 26, 2026. [source]
note: Exact-model US dealer operation guide distinguishes stopped fine-to-coarse adjustment from motor-running coarse-to-fine return and jam recovery.
